name: Sinking of Cruiser Moskva
detail: Ukraine's R-360 Neptune anti-ship missiles strike and sink the Russian Black Sea Fleet flagship Moskva on April 13-14, 2022. Largest warship destroyed in combat since 1982. Forces Russia to withdraw fleet from northwestern Black Sea.

name: Kerch Bridge Strike (Oct 2022)
detail: Massive explosion on the Kerch Strait Bridge on Putin's 70th birthday disrupts critical supply line to Crimea. Two road sections collapse; fuel tanker fire on rail section. Russia responds with mass missile strikes on Ukrainian cities.

name: Kharkiv Oblast Counteroffensive
detail: Ukraine's surprise armored offensive in September 2022 liberates over 8,000 sq km in Kharkiv Oblast in days, including the key logistics hub of Izium. Russia's largest defeat since the failed Kyiv offensive. Evidence of torture chambers found in liberated areas.

name: Liberation of Kherson City
detail: Ukraine liberates Kherson city on November 11, 2022 as Russia retreats across the Dnipro River. First occupied regional capital retaken. Zelensky visits the liberated city within 24 hours.

name: Naval Drone Campaign vs Black Sea Fleet
detail: Ukraine's campaign of naval drone attacks on the Black Sea Fleet (2022-2024) damaged or sank multiple Russian warships, ultimately forcing Russia to relocate its fleet from Sevastopol to Novorossiysk. The degraded fleet enabled Ukraine to resume partial Black Sea shipping.

name: Kursk Oblast Incursion
detail: Ukraine's August 2024 cross-border incursion into Russia's Kursk Oblast captured 1,000+ sq km including Sudzha. First foreign military occupation of Russian soil since WWII. Forced Russia to divert forces from Donbas and embarrassed Putin domestically.

name: HIMARS Strikes on Russian Ammunition Depots
detail: From June 2022, Ukraine used US-supplied HIMARS rockets to destroy Russian ammunition depots behind front lines. Over 400 confirmed strikes on high-value targets. Significantly reduced Russian artillery fire rates and disrupted logistics. Russia relocated most large depots beyond HIMARS range (70km).

name: Storm Shadow Strike Sinks Novocherkassk Landing Ship
detail: Ukraine used UK-supplied Storm Shadow cruise missiles to strike and sink the Russian landing ship Novocherkassk in Feodosia harbor, Crimea, on December 26, 2023. The third Russian landing ship sunk or severely damaged in Crimean ports, further degrading Russia's naval amphibious capability.

name: Bayraktar TB2 Drone Campaign (Early War)
detail: Ukraine's Bayraktar TB2 combat drones proved devastatingly effective in the first weeks of the war (Feb-April 2022), destroying hundreds of Russian vehicles, artillery systems, and an air defense radar. TB2's effectiveness forced Russia to strengthen air defense, and the drone became a symbol of Ukrainian resistance globally.

name: SBU Alpha Strikes Lukoil Perm Refinery — 1,500 km Deep Strike
detail: Ukraine's SBU Alpha special operations center struck the Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez refinery in Perm, Russia on April 30, 2026 — one of the deepest strikes of the entire war at over 1,500 km from Ukrainian-held territory. The SBU hit the AVT-4 primary refining unit, setting vacuum and atmospheric distillation columns ablaze and 'effectively putting the unit out of operation.' At least four 50,000-cubic-meter crude storage tanks also burned. A chemical emergency alert was issued in Perm. The facility processes ~13 million metric tons of crude annually. The Perm linear production-dispatch station (Transneft-operated) was also struck for the second consecutive day, further disrupting Russia's petroleum supply chain.

name: Ukraine's Largest-Ever Drone Attack — ~556 Drones Strike Moscow Region; Refinery, Airports, Transneft Targeted
detail: Overnight into May 17, 2026, Ukraine launched its largest drone attack of the entire war against Russia, sending approximately 556 drones at Moscow and surrounding regions. Fires erupted at a Moscow oil refinery and Transneft oil-pumping stations in Moscow Oblast; the ELMA Technopark was struck; and drone debris fell on Sheremetyevo Airport — Russia's busiest — causing roughly 200 flight delays and cancellations, with 100 more at Vnukovo. At least 4 people were killed (3 in Moscow region, 1 in Belgorod Oblast) and 12+ wounded. Ukraine's SBU confirmed the joint Armed Forces/SBU operation, targeting military-industrial and fuel infrastructure. President Zelensky called it 'entirely justified — a completely fair response' to Russia's killing of Ukrainian civilians. The attack broke the record for the largest Ukrainian drone barrage, previously 389 drones (March 2026), and demonstrated Ukraine's ability to sustain large-scale deep strikes even while absorbing Russian attacks at home.

name: Ukraine Strikes Afipsky and Novoshakhtinsk Oil Refineries — 2 Killed
detail: Overnight into August 25, 2026, Ukrainian long-range drones struck Russia's Afipsky oil refinery in Krasnodar Krai (about 375 km from the front line), sparking a major fire. Krasnodar Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said falling drone debris killed 2 people and injured 2 others near the Afipsky railway station, and damaged at least 10 private homes in the town of Afipsky. The same night, Ukrainian forces also struck the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery in Rostov Oblast and the Astrakhan gas processing plant. Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service linked the sustained refinery campaign to a 19% drop in Russian wheat export prices.

name: Ukraine Hits 16 Targets Across Russia, Destroys Wildberries Warehouse — 3 Killed
detail: President Zelensky said Ukrainian forces struck 16 targets across Russia over the past day into August 26, 2026, including oil facilities, logistics hubs, airfields, a missile unit, a military enterprise, and infrastructure Russia uses to launch attacks on Ukraine. A Wildberries logistics center in Kotovsk, Tambov Oblast was 'completely destroyed by fire' across roughly 100,000 square meters, per Tambov Governor Yevgeny Pervyshov, injuring 1 person. Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a strike on Lukoil's NORSI oil refinery in Nizhny Novgorod Oblast. Separate drone strikes killed a man and a 14-year-old in Lipetsk Oblast and a woman in Belgorod Oblast. Russia's Defense Ministry claimed 426 Ukrainian drones were intercepted overnight.
